source.title: GRAB: An LLM-Inspired Sequence-First Click-Through Rate Prediction Modeling Paradigm
source.authors: Shao-Peng Chen; Chuyue Xie; Hui-Min Ren; Shaozong Zhang; Han Zhang; R. Cheng; Zhi-Qiang Cao; Zehao Ju; Yu Gao; Jie Ding; Xiaodong Chen; Xuewu Jiao; Shuang Li; Liu Lin

record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates scaling behavior in a new setting—a recommendation model—by varying model capacity and behavior-sequence length. It does not test language-model pretraining loss or the original scaling-law measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper cites language-model and recommendation scaling laws, but cited results are not rows. Its own relevant results are CTR AUC trends across GRAB capacity settings and behavior-sequence lengths; it does not fit power laws or report held-out language-model cross-entropy.
record.test_reason: An industrial CTR recommendation model (GRAB) cites LLM scaling laws as motivation and reports its own AUC trends across 8 capacity configurations (6.48M–11.27M params, under 2x) and across behavior-sequence lengths. No held-out loss, no power-law fit, no extrapolation, no compute allocation, and no span of orders of magnitude. The trends measure a related construct (CTR AUC versus a capacity or sequence-length setting), so they go under fits_no_version rather than testing V5. It is borderline T3 for V5, but the power-law form V5 names is never examined.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that scaling analysis shows continued AUC gains from larger models and longer sequences, with no saturation in the tested range. They describe the sequence-length gain as monotonic and approximately linear and frame this as LLM-like scaling behavior. They fit no scaling law and measure no language-model loss.
record.recipe_differences: This is supervised CTR prediction in a recommendation model, with AUC as the outcome; it does not use the original language-model held-out-loss scaling measurement or fit power laws.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported CTR performance changes with model-capacity configuration and behavior-sequence length.

fits_no_version.finding: GRAB test AUC rises across 8 capacity configurations (6.48M–11.27M params) varying layers, heads and d_model. The authors report no significant saturation in the tested range (Fig. 6b, Table 2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In generative CTR recommenders, AUC improves monotonically with model capacity over small parameter ranges.

fits_no_version.finding: GRAB AUC improves monotonically, described as approximately linearly, with longer user behavior sequences. Its gains over baselines grow with sequence length (Fig. 6a).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In generative CTR recommenders, AUC improves with the length of the modeled behavior sequence.

record.problems: The scaling outcomes are reported as AUC, not held-out language-model cross-entropy. The tested parameter range is 6.48M–11.27M, and no exponents, power-law fits, extrapolation tests, or compute-optimal allocations are reported. Exact scaling values are available only in figures, not stated in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No other claim-relevant results left out. The paper's overall model comparisons, component ablations, and online CTR/CPM results do not measure the scaling behavior recorded here.

untested.parts: No held-out pretraining loss of language models; no power-law sweep over parameters, tokens or compute.
No fits on small runs extrapolated to larger ones.
Depth and head variations at near-constant parameter count are run, but only AUC appears in a figure, with no loss and no textual values.
The recommendation setting is new, but no power-law form is fitted or tested; only monotonic AUC gains over a range under 2x.
No downstream predictability from scale or loss for language models.
No comparison of fitting choices or exponents.

missing.what: Table 1 reports GRAB-small at AUC 0.83661 and GRAB-standard at 0.83772, a size comparison with exact values. The sizes of the two variants are not stated. This is not linked to any version but is the only numeric size contrast.

record.verdict_notes: This is a recommendation-systems paper; scaling is a side analysis. The capacity sweep spans under 2x in parameters, and all scaling values are figure-only. It is not an original source. The reader's 'tests/T3' with all versions not_tested is internally inconsistent; reclassified as uses_without_test/T4.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out language-model pretraining loss sweep over parameters, tokens, or compute.
No small-run fits or predictions of substantially larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or compute-optimal parameter/token scaling.
The architecture configurations do not hold parameter count fixed, and the study reports CTR AUC rather than held-out loss.
The study evaluates a recommendation model, but does not test whether the same power-law form holds in another modality or training regime.
It measures recommendation CTR AUC, not downstream-task performance of language models or its relation to pretraining loss.
No alternative fitting choices, exponents, compute-optimal splits, or departures from fitted power-law curves are compared.

rows.subject: GRAB
rows.stage_stated: Supervised CTR prediction; trained to minimize binary cross-entropy.
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated CTR AUC across model-capacity configurations that vary Transformer layers, attention heads, and feature dimension.
rows.note: The paper states that increasing model capacity improves performance and reports no significant saturation in the tested range. Exact per-configuration AUC values are not stated in the text; this row records the aggregate trend.
rows.check: The measure is CTR AUC, not loss. The parameter range is under 2x and values appear only in Fig. 6b, so no power-law form can be read. Configurations that change depth or heads barely change parameters (6.48–6.83M), which resembles a shape sweep. But per-configuration AUC is not given in text and AUC is not loss, so this cannot support V4. The 'observed' state applies only to the authors' monotonic-improvement statement, not to any version.

rows.subject: GRAB
rows.stage_stated: Supervised CTR prediction; trained to minimize binary cross-entropy.
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated CTR performance at varying user behavior-sequence lengths.

conditions.value: Varying user behavior-sequence lengths; exact lengths not stated

rows.note: The paper states that GRAB's performance gains become more pronounced as sequence length increases and describes its AUC as improving monotonically with longer sequences. Exact per-length values are not stated in the text.
rows.check: This row compares GRAB with other models across sequence lengths (Fig. 6a); part of it is the study's own method versus baselines. It reports no power law in data or tokens; the abstract calls the improvement 'approximately linear'. The exact lengths and values are not given.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
